tools.name: whoami
tools.title: Who is connected
tools.description: The account this connection works with: a Back4App account, a temporary account (with its deadline and claim link), or none yet. Tells which account the other tools act on.

tools.name: create_temporary_account
tools.title: Go on without an account
tools.description: Starts a temporary Back4App account for a connection with no account; refused on one that has an account. It lasts 24 hours and holds one app on the Free plan, deployed from a folder. The person keeps the app by opening the claim link and signing in; otherwise everything is deleted at the deadline. The answer has the claim link, which the person opens to keep the app.

tools.name: sign_in
tools.title: Sign in to Back4App
tools.description: Connects the person's Back4App account: the client opens the browser for them to sign in (or create an account) and approve. For when the person wants their own account, or when a temporary account is over. The call itself is cut short by the sign-in; the tools work with the account once the client says it is connected.

tools.name: list_web_apps
tools.title: List apps
tools.description: The account's web apps, its own and the ones it collaborates on, newest first: state, URL, plan, where the code comes from and the last deployment. On the Free plan, urlExpiresAt is when the URL stops answering (a deploy after that brings the app back at a new URL); offlineReason says why an app is OFFLINE. The first step when working with an app that exists.

cursor.description: nextCursor of the page before, for the one that follows.

tools.name: get_web_app
tools.title: Get an app
tools.description: One app in full: where its code comes from, root folder, builder, port, start command, health check, plan, URL, the names of its environment variables and its last deployment. On the Free plan, urlExpiresAt is when the URL stops answering (a deploy after that brings the app back at a new URL); offlineReason says why an app is OFFLINE (FREE_ADDRESS_EXPIRED: that time passed, not a failed deploy).

appId.description: The id of the app, from list_web_apps.

tools.name: create_web_app
tools.title: Create an app and deploy it
tools.description: Creates an app on the Free plan from a folder of code and starts its first deployment. The app must listen on the port given in the PORT environment variable. Send the code one way: uploadId and manifestSha256 (from the command create_upload gives, when there is a terminal) or files (the code in this call, when there is none). For an app that exists, deploy_web_app and update_web_app send new code.

name.description: The app's name. Usually the folder's name.

path.description: Relative to the folder, with forward slashes.

encoding.description: utf-8 by default; base64 for binary files.

files.description: The code itself, for a client with no terminal: at most 200 files and 5 MB in all. Leave out dependencies and build output (node_modules, dist, .venv) and .env files. With a terminal, use create_upload instead.

uploadId.description: Printed by the command create_upload gave.

manifestSha256.description: Printed next to the uploadId, by the same command.

rootDir.description: The folder of the app inside the code. "./" by default.

builder.description: DOCKERFILE when the code has a Dockerfile, BUILDPACK otherwise, by default.

startCommand.description: Only for BUILDPACK. Detected from the code by default.

port.description: The port the app listens on. The app should read it from the PORT environment variable.

healthCheckPath.description: A path that answers 2xx once the app is up. "/" by default.

envVars.description: Environment variables. Their values are never read back by any tool.

tools.name: update_web_app
tools.title: Change an app and deploy it again
tools.description: Changes an app's settings or environment variables and always deploys it again; only what is sent changes. New code can go along with the change. To deploy with nothing else changed, use deploy_web_app. The first call changes nothing: it answers a summary of the change (the variables by name) and a confirmationId. Show the summary to the person and, if they agree, call update_web_app again with the same arguments and the confirmationId.

appId.description: The id of the app, from list_web_apps.

rootDir.description: The folder of the app inside the code. "./" by default.

builder.description: DOCKERFILE when the code has a Dockerfile, BUILDPACK otherwise, by default.

startCommand.description: Only for BUILDPACK. Detected from the code by default.

port.description: The port the app listens on. The app should read it from the PORT environment variable.

healthCheckPath.description: A path that answers 2xx once the app is up. "/" by default.

envVars.description: Sets these variables and leaves the others as they are. The values are never read back.

path.description: Relative to the folder, with forward slashes.

encoding.description: utf-8 by default; base64 for binary files.

files.description: The code itself, for a client with no terminal: at most 200 files and 5 MB in all. Leave out dependencies and build output (node_modules, dist, .venv) and .env files. With a terminal, use create_upload instead.

uploadId.description: Printed by the command create_upload gave.

manifestSha256.description: Printed next to the uploadId, by the same command.

confirmationId.description: From the first call, once the person agreed: the same change runs.

tools.name: create_upload
tools.title: Get the command that sends a folder
tools.description: For a client with a terminal: gives the command that packs the project's folder and sends it to Back4App. Run the command in the folder; it needs no login and prints the uploadId and manifestSha256 that create_web_app, deploy_web_app and update_web_app take. Pass appId when the code is for an app that exists.

appId.description: The app the code is for, when it exists already.

tools.name: deploy_web_app
tools.title: Deploy an app
tools.description: Publishes new code to an app, or deploys its latest code again when no code is sent. Send new code as uploadId and manifestSha256 (from create_upload, called with this appId) or as files.

appId.description: The id of the app, from list_web_apps.

path.description: Relative to the folder, with forward slashes.

encoding.description: utf-8 by default; base64 for binary files.

files.description: The code itself, for a client with no terminal: at most 200 files and 5 MB in all. Leave out dependencies and build output (node_modules, dist, .venv) and .env files. With a terminal, use create_upload instead.

uploadId.description: Printed by the command create_upload gave.

manifestSha256.description: Printed next to the uploadId, by the same command.

tools.name: get_deployment
tools.title: Follow a deployment
tools.description: One deployment: status (QUEUED, BUILDING, DEPLOYING, READY, FAILED, CANCELED or REMOVED), phase, dates, source, and the URL once READY. When FAILED it brings the error and the end of the build log. When the analysis of the code found settings the app does not have (environment variables, start command, port), it brings them as suggestions. When the app was not listening on the port its settings named, portDetected says where it was found: the port setting of the app was changed to that one, so tell the person. Follows a deployment started by create_web_app, deploy_web_app, update_web_app or a confirmed rollback, until it is READY or FAILED.

deploymentId.description: From create_web_app, deploy_web_app, update_web_app, confirm_action or list_deployments.

tools.name: list_deployments
tools.title: List deployments
tools.description: An app's deployments, newest first. Use it to find an older deployment, or the one a push to the repository started.

appId.description: The id of the app, from list_web_apps.

cursor.description: nextCursor of the page before, for the one that follows.

tools.name: rollback
tools.title: Ask to roll an app back
tools.description: Asks to put an app back on its previous version, when the new one misbehaves and the one before worked. Nothing changes on this call: it answers a summary of the swap and a confirmationId. Show the summary to the person and, if they agree, call confirm_action. Environment variables and the database stay as they are.

appId.description: The id of the app, from list_web_apps.

tools.name: confirm_action
tools.title: Confirm an operation
tools.description: Runs an operation that was waiting for a confirmation, such as a rollback, after its summary was shown to the person. A confirmationId lasts 5 minutes and works once.

confirmationId.description: From the tool that asked for the confirmation.

tools.name: get_build_logs
tools.title: Read build logs
tools.description: The log of a deployment, oldest line first: fetching the code, the build, pushing the image, starting the container and the health check. The app's latest deployment by default. Read it when a deployment is FAILED.

appId.description: The id of the app, from list_web_apps.

deploymentId.description: The app's latest deployment by default.

tail.description: How many of the last lines. 100 by default.

tools.name: get_runtime_logs
tools.title: Read runtime logs
tools.description: What the app's running container wrote, oldest line first. The platform keeps the last 100 lines. Read it when a deployment is READY but the app misbehaves.

appId.description: The id of the app, from list_web_apps.

tail.description: How many of the last lines. 100 by default.
